about: Research record for the FairPay incentive rule knowledge base. Read ONLY by incentive_kb_ingest.py, which writes these rules to Qdrant; the incentive audit never reads this file. Every stored field has an evidence quote. A field no source documents is left out and is stored as NOT_DOCUMENTED; a likely behaviour with no source goes in 'inferences', which the deterministic engine never uses. Research round 2, retrieved 2026-10-08.

source_tiers.1: Official platform documentation, websites, filings and app listings published by the platform itself
source_tiers.2: Reputable journalism directly reporting an actual offer, and published research
source_tiers.3: Real-world rider evidence (public screenshots, videos, rider reports)
source_tiers.4: Third-party blogs, SEO articles and aggregators

not_ingested.claim: Uber Eats incentive rules for India
not_ingested.reason: Not a rule but a geography finding. Zomato's and Uber's own announcement of 21 January 2020 states Uber Eats discontinued operations in India and directed its delivery partners to Zomato. Uber's FY2020 Form 10-K confirms the divestiture. No Uber Eats India incentive therefore exists after that date, so every Uber Quest rule in this record is stored with region 'United States' and is never labelled India.

not_ingested.claim: Swiggy daily order-count slabs (e.g. 15/20/25 orders for fixed bonuses), '40 hours a week' login duration, 'order rejection below 5%', Swiggy Instamart slabs of 16/22/28 orders for Rs 160-520, Blinkit daily milestones of 18/24/30 orders for Rs 200-550, Zomato daily targets of 12/20/28 orders for Rs 150/350/600, Zomato '95% login compliance' in booked gig slots
not_ingested.reason: Not stored as rules. These are unbylined third-party SEO pages that cite no source, and their figures differ between their own articles. Storing them would let the deterministic engine produce findings from numbers no platform, journalist or rider has corroborated. The claims are instead attached as LOW-confidence 'inferences' on the official documents for the same programmes, where the engine ignores them and a reader can still see them.

not_ingested.claim: Per-order rates and incentive shares for quick commerce (about Rs 12.18 per km, Rs 2.9 per minute, incentives about 23.5% of weekly earnings, one worker at about 90 orders for Rs 2,537 with Rs 828 of incentives per week)
not_ingested.reason: Read in full (GigSaathi / the internet Research Lab, 'Forced Volatility: Earnings and Incentives for Gig Work in Quick Commerce'). It reports aggregate regression results and per-order averages, not any incentive's target, reward or eligibility conditions, so it yields no rule fields. Its finding that platforms do not publish advance rate cards or incentives is recorded as context in the report.

not_ingested.claim: Swiggy rejection penalty of Rs 10 a week for rejecting four to ten orders in a week; Swiggy shift types (part-time 8pm-3am, full-time 11am-11pm, ultra full-time 7am-11pm) with mandatory weekends
not_ingested.reason: Reputable journalism (Scroll.in, 15 December 2018) but it describes a penalty and shift structure, not an incentive's eligibility conditions, and it is eight years old. Recorded in the report as evidence that rejections affect pay; not stored as a rule.

rules.incentive_name: Swiggy 'Double Earnings' New Year's Eve offer
rules.source_title: Gig workers strike fizzles out in Bengaluru (Deccan Herald)
rules.source_reference: a Swiggy offer in Bengaluru reported by Deccan Herald on 31 Dec 2025
rules.description: A one-day promotional offer in Bengaluru on New Year's Eve: 19 orders between 6 pm and midnight for Rs 2,175, with at most one order rejected in that window.

evidence.quote: Swiggy ran a promotional ‘Double Earnings’ offer, advertising earnings of Rs 2,175 for 19 orders, within a period of six hours between 6 pm and 12 am.
The gig workers had the option of rejecting only one order during the time period.
To encourage delivery professionals, platforms, like Swiggy and Zomato rolled out heightened incentives across the city.
evidence.note: The report is datelined Bengaluru, so the offer is stored as a Bengaluru offer and not as a nationwide rule.

inferences.inferred_behaviour: Not documented for this offer. Whether each order of a batched trip counts towards the 19 is unknown.
inferences.basis: No source states a counting rule for this campaign.

notes: A single-day campaign in one city, reported during a nationwide gig worker strike. It is evidence of one observed offer, not a standing Swiggy rule.
The reward is the offer's advertised total earnings for the 19 orders, which may include base pay rather than being a bonus on top.
